The winner will serve in the [[United States House of Representatives]] for the remainder of the [[119th United States Congress]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/06/nyregion/new-jersey-special-election-malinowski-mejia.html |access-date=February 7, 2026 |title=In a Close Election, Voters Send a Sharp Anti-Trump Message |first=Tracey |last=Tully |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 6, 2026}} The seat became vacant on November 20, 2025, when [[Mikie Sherrill]] resigned to become the [[governor of New Jersey]]. Outgoing governor [[Phil Murphy]] announced the special election scheduled for April 16, 2026.{{cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/mikie-sherrill-is-now-a-former-congresswoman-as-n-j-awaits-writ-of-special-election/|title=Mikie Sherrill is now a former congresswoman as N.J. awaits writ of special election|last=Wildstein|first=David|date=November 20, 2025|access-date=November 20, 2025|website=[[New Jersey Globe]]}} Early voting took place from April 6 to April 14. Voters had the option to cast their [[Postal voting|votes by mail]].{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Joey |date=November 21, 2025 |title=Murphy sets February 5 primary, April 16 general for NJ-11 special election |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/murphy-sets-february-5-primary-april-16-general-for-nj-11-special-election/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=New Jersey Globe |language=en-US}} Primary elections were held on February 5, 2026. [[Analilia Mejia]], co-executive director of the [[Center for Popular Democracy]], won the Democratic nomination. [[Randolph, New Jersey|Randolph]] councilman and former mayor Joe Hathaway won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nomination uncontested.{{Cite web |last=Martinez |first=Marissa |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Analilia Mejia wins New Jersey special election primary |url=https://19thnews.org/2026/02/analilia-mejia-new-jersey-primary/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260217163719/https://19thnews.org/2026/02/analilia-mejia-new-jersey-primary/ |archive-date=February 17, 2026 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The 19th]]}}{{Cite web |last=The Associated Press |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Malinowski concedes to Mejia in Democratic US House special primary in New Jersey |url=https://newjersey.news12.com/analilia-mejia-wins-democratic-primary-for-11th-district-special-election |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260307205246/https://newjersey.news12.com/analilia-mejia-wins-democratic-primary-for-11th-district-special-election |archive-date=March 7, 2026 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=NJ News 12}} Mejia would then go on to win the special election; her win was the best Democratic performance since [[1982 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 11|1982]], the last time a Democrat won the district before [[2018 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 11|2018]].https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-special-elections/new-jersey-house-results ==Democratic primary== ===Campaign=== Spending by [[AIPAC]] against former U.S. Representative [[Tom Malinowski]] became a major issue in the primary.
